agent_notes: The Hebrew verse 1 includes the superscription; KJV and the other versions number it 145:0 and start the psalm at 145:1 after it. I translate the Hebrew verse as one unit and say so in the commentary.

STEPBible glosses אֱלוֹהַי as 'O God my' and links it to deity.yhwh; I glossed it 'my God' (the entity link is the packet's, not mine). Radak's remark that 'the name is written and not read' refers to the Ketiv/Qere of the divine name, which I did not use because the claim concerns the Hebrew form, not this verse's sense.

I did not use 'saints' for חסידיך in the translations: the word is about covenant loyalty (ḥesed), and 'saints' carries later Christian associations. Radak also reads it as 'those who go beyond' in contemplating God's works; I kept that reading out of the translations and used it only in the commentary, as his own interpretation.

The packet shows the pronoun in the verse shifting from 'your' (v.11) to 'his' (v.12) mid-sentence. Meiri says this is the prophets' habit of switching between second and third person; I kept the Hebrew shift in the literal layer and smoothed it in the dramatic layer.

Addressed the request: the last sentence of the commentary now gives Ibn Ezra's point that the vav of gevurotav (the 'his' suffix) refers back to 'the glory of your kingdom' in verse 11, which accounts for the shift from 'your' to 'his'. Meiri's separate remark (prophetic style moves between second and third person) is kept as his own.

agent_notes: יְשַׂבֵּרוּ is Piel of שׂבר 'to hope, look expectantly' (BDB), not שׁבר 'to break'. STEPBible gives 'they wait'; I glossed 'they look expectantly'. The five English versions agree on 'wait / look'. Meaning of 'meat' in KJV is archaic 'food'.

Reviewer request addressed: the literal layer no longer uses a genitive. Hebrew has lekhol ('to/for every') with chai, then ratzon as a separate noun; I render 'satisfying to every living [thing] favour/desire' and gloss token 5 'to every' and token 6 'living [thing]'. The five English versions (KJV, YLT, ASV, Webster) all read 'the desire of every living thing'; BBE restructures as 'every living thing has its desire in full measure'. I keep the traditional sense 'desire' in the dramatic layer, as the commentators (Radak, Meiri, Metzudat David, Ibn Ezra) take it, and flag 'favour' as the other live reading of ratzon.

Malbim's reading (ratzon as the abstract subject that opens God's hand) is quoted from the packet as an outlier and is not adopted in the translation. The Rashi note contains an Old French gloss (אפיימנ״ט) that I did not try to decode or cite.

agent_notes: KJV 'holy' for חָסִיד is a harmonizing choice; the word is 'loyal, committed to covenant love' (ḥesed). I used 'loyal' in the literal layer; the packet's STEPBible 'faithful' is retained in the gloss. The same word is in the nun line in v13.

BBE 'give honour to his name' for 'call to him' is an interpretive paraphrase, noted in the commentary. Radak and Ibn Ezra differ on whether 'in truth' limits the promise (only sincere callers) or defines a sincere heart; I follow the plain sense and mention the sincerity reading.
I read the verbs as habitual imperfects ('he does/hears/saves'), as YLT does, rather than KJV's future 'will'. The ordering desire, cry, save is kept.
